6.h: 2 - Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿAmr al-Taymī * (ع)
6.t:
ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd ibn Taym ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah al-Qurashī, al-Taymī, al-Makkī, Abū Muḥammad. ⟦1:23⟧
One of the Ten Promised Paradise (العشرة المبشرة); he has a number of hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ.
He has in (Musnad Baqī ibn Makhlad), counting repetitions: thirty-eight hadiths.
He has two hadiths agreed upon (المتفق عليه); al-Bukhārī alone has two hadiths from him, and Muslim alone three hadiths (1) .
Narrating from him: بنوه؛ يحيى، وموسى، وعيسى، والسائب بن يزيد، ومالك بن أوس بن الحدثان، وأبو عثمان النهدي، وقيس بن أبي حازم، ومالك بن أبي عامر الأصبحي، والأحنف بن قيس التميمي، وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن، وآخرون.
Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mandah said: He was a dark-complexioned man with abundant hair, neither tightly curled nor lank, handsome of face; when he walked he walked quickly, and he did not dye his hair (2) .
Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir al-Ḥizāmī said: عن عبد العزيز بن عمران، حدثني ⟦1:24⟧ إسحاق بن يحيى، حدثني موسى بن طلحة، قال:
My father was white tinged with redness, of medium build, nearer to short, broad-chested, wide between the shoulders, with large feet; when he turned, he turned with his whole body (1) .
I say: He was among those who were first to Islam (2) , and he was harmed for the sake of Allah, then he emigrated. It happened that he was absent from the Battle of Badr on a trading journey of his in Syria (3) , and he was pained at his absence, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ allotted him his share and his reward (4) .
Abū al-Qāsim ibn ʿAsākir the hadith master (الحافظ) said in his biography: He was with ʿUmar when he came to al-Jābiyah, and he put him in charge of the Muhājirūn.
Someone else said: His hand was paralysed from shielding the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with it on the Day of Uḥud.
الصلت بن دينار: عن أبي نضرة، عن جابر، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever ⟦1:25⟧ wishes to look at a martyr walking on his two feet, let him look at Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh (1)) .
أخبرنيه الأبرقوهي، أنبأنا ابن أبي الجود، أنبأنا ابن الطلابة، أنبأنا عبد العزيز الأنماطي، أنبأنا أبو طاهر المخلص، حدثنا البغوي، حدثنا داود بن رشيد (2) ، حدثنا مكي، حدثنا الصلت.
And in (Jāmiʿ Abī ʿĪsā), with a sound (الحسن) chain of transmission (الإسناد):
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the Day of Uḥud: (Ṭalḥah has made it binding (3)) .
Ibn Abī Khālid said: عن قيس، قال:
I saw the hand of Ṭalḥah with which he shielded the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Uḥud: it was paralysed.
Recorded by: al-Bukhārī (4) . ⟦1:26⟧
And al-Nasāʾī recorded, from the hadith of يحيى بن أيوب وآخر، عن عمارة بن غزية، عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر، قال:
On the Day of Uḥud, when the people turned and fled, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was to one side with twelve men, among them Ṭalḥah, and the polytheists caught up with them.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Who will take on these people?) .
Ṭalḥah said: I will.
He said: (Stay as you are) .
A man said: I will.
He said: (You) .
He fought until he was killed. Then he turned, and there (1) were the polytheists.
He said: (Who will take them on?) .
Ṭalḥah said: I will.
He said: (Stay as you are) .
A man of the Anṣār said: I will.
He said: (You) .
He fought until he was killed, and it went on like that until only Ṭalḥah remained with the Prophet of Allah.
He said: (Who will take on these people?) .
Ṭalḥah said: I will.
Ṭalḥah fought as the eleven had fought, until his fingers were cut off.
He said: Ḥass!
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Had you said: In the name of Allah, the angels would have lifted you up while the people looked on) .
Then Allah drove back the polytheists (2) .
Its narrators are reliable (ثقة).
أخبرنا أبو المعالي بن أبي عصرون الشافعي، أنبأنا عبد المعز بن محمد في كتابه، أنبأنا تميم بن أبي سعيد، أنبأنا محمد بن عبد الرحمن، أنبأنا محمد بن أحمد، أنبأنا أحمد (3) بن علي التميمي، حدثنا محمد بن أبي بكر المقدمي، وعبد الأعلى، قال:
حدثنا المعتمر، سمعت أبي، حدثنا أبو عثمان، ⟦1:27⟧ قال: In some of those days in which the Messenger of Allah fought, none remained with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except Ṭalḥah and Saʿd, according to the account of the two of them (1) .
Recorded by: the two Shaykhs, from al-Muqaddamī.
And with the same chain to al-Tamīmī: حدثنا أبو كريب، حدثنا يونس بن بكير، عن طلحة بن يحيى، عن موسى وعيسى ابني طلحة، عن أبيهما:
that the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a Bedouin who had come to ask him about the one who had fulfilled his vow: Who is he?
They did not dare to question him ﷺ, out of reverence and awe for him.
The Bedouin asked him, and he turned away from him; then he asked him again, and he turned away from him. Then I appeared at the door of the mosque - wearing green garments -.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me, he said: (Where is the one who asked about the one who had fulfilled his vow?) .
The Bedouin said: Here I am.
He said: (This man is among those who have fulfilled their vow (2)) .
And it was recorded by: al-Ṭayālisī in his (Musnad), from the hadith of Muʿāwiyah.
He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Ṭalḥah is among those who have fulfilled their vow) (3) . ⟦1:28⟧
And in (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim), from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on Ḥirāʾ, he, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah and al-Zubayr, and the rock moved.
The Messenger of Allah said: (Be still! For upon you there is none but a prophet, or a man of truth, or a martyr) (1) .
سويد بن سعيد: حدثنا صالح بن موسى، عن معاوية بن إسحاق، عن عائشة بنت طلحة، عن عائشة:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever would be pleased to look at a man walking on the earth who has fulfilled his vow, let him look at Ṭalḥah (2)) .
al-Tirmidhī said: حدثنا أبو سعيد الأشج، حدثنا أبو عبد الرحمن نضر بن منصور، حدثنا عقبة بن علقمة اليشكري، سمعت عليا يوم الجمل يقول:
I heard from the mouth (3) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: (Ṭalḥah and al-Zubayr are my two neighbours in Paradise (4)) .
Likewise it was narrated by: Ibn Zaydān al-Bajalī and Abū Bakr al-Jārūdī, from al-Ashajj.
And Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī was anomalous (الشاذ), and said: عن نضر، عن أبيه، عن عقبة. ⟦1:29⟧
دحيم: حدثنا محمد بن طلحة، عن موسى بن محمد، عن أبيه، عن سلمة بن الأكوع، قال:
Ṭalḥah bought a well near the mountain, slaughtered a camel and fed the people; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (You are Ṭalḥah al-Fayyāḍ (1)) .
سليمان بن أيوب بن عيسى بن موسى بن طلحة: حدثني أبي (2) ، عن جدي، عن موسى بن طلحة، عن أبيه، قال:
On the Day of Uḥud the Prophet ﷺ named him: Ṭalḥah al-Khayr; at the expedition of Dhū al-ʿUshayrah (3) : Ṭalḥah al-Fayyāḍ; and on the Day of Khaybar: Ṭalḥah al-Jūd (4) .
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is soft in hadith (لين الحديث).
Mujālid said: عن الشعبي، عن قبيصة بن جابر، قال:
I kept company with Ṭalḥah, and I never saw anyone who gave abundant wealth more readily without being asked (5) .
أبو إسماعيل الترمذي: حدثنا سليمان بن أيوب بن سليمان بن عيسى بن موسى، حدثني أبي، عن جدي، عن موسى، عن أبيه:
that wealth came to him from ⟦1:30⟧ Ḥaḍramawt, seven hundred thousand, and he spent his night tossing and turning.
His wife said to him: What is the matter with you?
He said: I have been thinking since nightfall, and I said: What does a man think of his Lord who spends the night with this wealth in his house?
She said: What keeps you from some of your close friends? When morning comes, call for large bowls and platters, and divide it.
He said to her: May Allah have mercy on you, you are one granted success, the daughter of one granted success. She was Umm Kulthūm bint al-Ṣiddīq.
When morning came, he called for large bowls and divided it among the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, and he sent a bowl of it to ʿAlī.
His wife said to him: Abū Muḥammad! Was there no share for us in this wealth?
He said: Where have you been all day? Take what remains.
She said: It was a purse containing about a thousand dirhams.
أخبرنا المسلم بن علان، وجماعة كتابة، قالوا:
أنبأنا عمر بن محمد، أنبأنا هبة الله بن الحصين، أنبأنا ابن غيلان، أنبأنا أبو بكر الشافعي، حدثنا إبراهيم الحربي، حدثنا عبد الله بن عمر، حدثنا محمد بن يعلى، حدثنا الحسن بن دينار، عن علي بن زيد، قال:
A Bedouin came to Ṭalḥah asking him for help, and sought to draw close to him through a tie of kinship.
He said: This is a tie of kinship by which no one before you has asked me. I have a piece of land for which ʿUthmān has offered me three hundred thousand; take it, or if you wish, I will sell it to ʿUthmān and hand you the price.
He said: The price.
So he gave it to him.
الكديمي (1) : حدثنا الأصمعي، حدثنا ابن عمران قاضي المدينة:
that Ṭalḥah ransomed ten of the captives of Badr with his own wealth; and once he was asked on the basis of kinship, and said:
I have sold a walled garden of mine for seven hundred thousand, and I have the option on it; if you wish, take it, or if you wish, its price.
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is broken (منقطع), besides al-Kudaymī being weak (ضعيف). ⟦1:31⟧
Ibn Saʿd said: أنبأنا سعيد بن منصور، حدثنا صالح بن موسى، عن معاوية بن إسحاق، عن عائشة، وأم إسحاق بنتي طلحة، قالتا:
Our father was wounded on the Day of Uḥud with twenty-four wounds. Among them, a square gash struck his head, his sciatic vein was severed - meaning the vein - his finger was paralysed, and the rest of the wounds were on his body. Fainting overcame him, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had his front tooth broken and his face gashed, and faintness had come over him; and Ṭalḥah was carrying him, retreating backwards with him; whenever any of the polytheists reached him, he fought in his defence, until he propped him up against the mountain pass (1) .
ابن عيينة: عن طلحة بن يحيى، حدثتني جدتي سعدى بنت عوف المرية، قالت:
I went in to Ṭalḥah one day while he was out of sorts (2) .
I said: What is the matter with you? Perhaps something from your family has troubled you?
He said: No, by Allah, and what an excellent wife of a Muslim you are! But some wealth I have has distressed me.
I said: What distresses you? Turn to your people.
He said: Boy! Call my people for me. And he divided it among them.
I asked the treasurer: How much did he give?
He said: Four hundred thousand (3) .
هشام، وعوف: عن الحسن البصري:
that Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh sold a piece of land of his for seven hundred thousand, and spent the night sleepless for fear of that wealth until morning, then he distributed it.
محمد بن سعد: حدثنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا موسى بن محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي، عن أبيه، قال:
Ṭalḥah used to draw a revenue of four hundred thousand from Iraq, and from al-Sarāh (4) ⟦1:32⟧ ten thousand dinars, or less, or more; and at al-Aʿrāḍ (1) he had revenues. He would not leave anyone of Banū Taym in need without providing for him and paying off his debt. He used to send ten thousand to ʿĀʾishah each year when his revenue came in, and he paid off thirty thousand on behalf of so-and-so (2) al-Taymī (3) .
al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me that Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh paid off eighty thousand dirhams on behalf of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Maʿmar and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz.
al-Ḥumaydī said: حدثنا ابن عيينة، حدثنا عمرو بن دينار، أخبرني مولى لطلحة، قال:
Ṭalḥah's revenue each day was a full thousand (4) .
al-Wāqidī said: حدثنا إسحاق بن يحيى، عن موسى بن طلحة: that Muʿāwiyah asked him: How much did Abū Muḥammad leave in cash?
He said: He left two million dirhams and two hundred thousand dirhams, and in gold two hundred thousand dinars.
Muʿāwiyah said: He lived praiseworthy, generous, ⟦1:33⟧ noble, and was killed lamented (1) , (may Allah have mercy on him) (2) .
And al-Riyāshī recited, from a man of Quraysh:
O you who ask me about the best of the servants ... you have come upon one of knowledge and experience
The best of all the servants are Quraysh ... and the best of Quraysh are the people of the Hijrah
And the best of the people of the Hijrah are the foremost ... eight, they alone a band of support
ʿAlī and ʿUthmān, then al-Zubayr ... and Ṭalḥah, and two from Zuhrah
And two righteous men who lay beside Aḥmad ... and his grave lies beside their grave
So whoever after them would boast ... let him not mention his boast after them
يحيى بن معين: حدثنا هشام بن يوسف، عن عبد الله بن مصعب، أخبرني موسى بن عقبة: سمعت علقمة بن وقاص الليثي، قال:
When Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr and ʿĀʾishah set out to seek vengeance for the blood of ʿUthmān, they turned aside on their way back at Dhāt ʿIrq, and considered ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān too young, so they sent them back.
He said: And I saw Ṭalḥah, and the gatherings dearest to him were the emptiest, while he had let his beard fall upon his chest, so I said:
O Abū Muḥammad! I see you, and the gatherings dearest to you are the emptiest; if you dislike this affair, leave it.
He said: O ʿAlqamah! Do not blame me. Yesterday we were one hand against those other than us, and today we have become two mountains of iron, each of us advancing on the other. But something came from me in the matter of ʿUthmān for which I see no expiation except the shedding of my blood in seeking vengeance for his (3) . ⟦1:34⟧
I say: What came from him concerning ʿUthmān was heedlessness and incitement, which he did through independent legal reasoning (الاجتهاد); then he changed when he witnessed the killing of ʿUthmān, and regretted abandoning his support (may Allah be pleased with both of them). And Ṭalḥah was the first to pledge allegiance to ʿAlī: the killers of ʿUthmān pressed him and brought him until he pledged allegiance.
al-Bukhārī said: حدثنا موسى بن أعين، حدثنا أبو عوانة، عن حصين في حديث عمرو بن جاوان، قال:
The two sides met on the Day of the Camel. Kaʿb ibn Sūr stood up with the copy of the Qurʾān, spread it open between the two parties, and adjured them by Allah and by Islam concerning their blood, and he kept at it until he was killed.
And Ṭalḥah was among the first killed (1) .
And al-Zubayr went off to join his sons, and was killed (2) .
يحيى القطان: عن عوف، حدثني أبو رجاء، قال:
I saw Ṭalḥah on his mount, saying: O people, be silent! But they began to swarm over him and would not be silent.
He said: Ugh! Moths of the Fire, and flies of greed (3) .
Ibn Saʿd said: أخبرني من سمع إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، عن حكيم بن جابر قال:
Ṭalḥah said: We were compliant in the matter of ʿUthmān, so today we find nothing better than to spend our blood for him. O Allah, take for ʿUthmān from me today until You are pleased (4) .
وكيع: حدثنا إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، عن قيس، قال:
I saw Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam when he shot Ṭalḥah that day with an arrow; it struck his knee, and it kept bleeding until ⟦1:35⟧ he died (1) .
A group narrated it from him; and the wording of ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Ṣāliḥ from him is: This one helped against ʿUthmān; I will not seek my revenge after today (2) .
I say: The killer of Ṭalḥah, in sin, is in the same position as the killer of ʿAlī.
Khalīfah ibn Khayyāṭ said: حدثنا من سمع جويرية بن أسماء، عن يحيى بن سعيد، عن عمه: that Marwān shot Ṭalḥah with an arrow and killed him, then turned to Abān and said:
We have spared you some of your father's killers (3) .
هشيم: عن مجالد، عن الشعبي، قال:
ʿAlī saw Ṭalḥah lying cast down in a valley; he dismounted, wiped the dust from his face, and said: It grieves me, Abū Muḥammad, to see you thrown down in the valleys beneath the stars of the sky. To Allah I complain of my ʿujar and my bujar.
al-Aṣmaʿī said: Its meaning is: my secrets and my sorrows that surge within me.
عبد الله بن إدريس: عن ليث، عن طلحة بن مصرف:
that ʿAlī came up to Ṭalḥah when he had died; he dismounted from his mount, sat him up, and wiped the dust from his face and his beard, ⟦1:36⟧ while asking for mercy upon him, and he said: Would that I had died twenty years before this day (1) .
Mursal (مرسل).
He narrated: زيد بن أبي أنيسة، عن محمد بن عبد الله من الأنصار، عن أبيه: that ʿAlī said: Give the killer of Ṭalḥah the tidings of the Fire.
أخبرنا ابن أبي عصرون، عن أبي روح، أنبأنا تميم، حدثنا أبو سعد، أنبأنا ابن حمدان، أنبأنا أبو يعلى، حدثنا عمرو الناقد، حدثنا الخضر بن محمد الحراني، حدثنا محمد بن سلمة، عن ابن إسحاق، عن محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي، عن مالك بن أبي عامر قال:
A man came to Ṭalḥah and said:
Have you considered this Yemeni: is he (2) more knowledgeable of the hadith of the Messenger of Allah than you - meaning Abū Hurayrah -? We hear from him things that we do not hear from you.
He said: As for his having heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what we did not hear, I have no doubt of it. I will tell you: we were people with households, and we would only come to the Messenger of Allah morning and evening, while he was a poor man with no wealth; he was always at the door of the Messenger of Allah. So I have no doubt that he heard what we did not hear. And do you find anyone in whom there is any good saying about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what he did not say (3) ?
Mujālid narrated: عن الشعبي، عن جابر: that he heard ʿUmar say to Ṭalḥah: Why is it ⟦1:37⟧ that I have seen you dishevelled and dusty since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died? Perhaps what troubles you is the leadership of your cousin - meaning Abū Bakr -.
He said: Allah forbid! I heard him say: (I know a word which no man says when death is present to him except that his soul finds rest in it when it leaves his body, and it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection) .
But I did not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he did not tell me of it; that is what has come over me.
ʿUmar said: I know it.
He said: Praise be to Allah! What is it?
He said: The word that he said to his uncle.
He said: You have spoken the truth (1) .
أبو معاوية، وغيره: حدثنا أبو مالك الأشجعي، عن أبي حبيبة (2) مولى لطلحة، قال:
I went in to ʿAlī with ʿImrān ibn Ṭalḥah after the Battle of the Camel; he welcomed him and drew him near, then said:
I hope that Allah will place me ⟦1:38⟧ and your father (1) among those of whom He said: “And We shall remove whatever rancour is in their breasts; as brothers, upon couches facing one another” [Qurʾān 15:47] .
Two men who were sitting there, one of them al-Ḥārith al-Aʿwar, said: Allah is more just than that He should accept them (2) and they should be brothers in Paradise.
He said: Get up, both of you, to the farthest and most remote land! Who then is it, if (3) it is not I and Ṭalḥah! O son of my brother: if you have any need, come to us (4) .
And from Abū Hurayrah:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (I saw myself on the Day of Uḥud with no one near me except Jibrīl on my right and Ṭalḥah on my left (5)) .
And it was said about that:
And Ṭalḥah, on the Day of the Pass, stood by Muḥammad ... in an hour that grew narrow upon him and was blocked
He shielded him from the spears with his two hands, so his fingers were cut ... beneath the spears and became paralysed
And he was the leader of the people after Muḥammad ... he set the millstone of Islam firm until it was settled
And from Ṭalḥah, who said: I was wounded on the Day of Uḥud over my whole body, even on my private part.
Ibn Saʿd (6) said: حدثنا محمد بن عمر، حدثني إسحاق بن يحيى، عن جدته سعدى بنت عوف، قالت: Ṭalḥah was killed while in the hands of his treasurer there were one million dirhams (7) , and two hundred ⟦1:39⟧ thousand dirhams, and his estates and real property were valued at thirty million dirhams (1) .
The strangest thing I have come across is the statement of Ibn al-Jawzī, in a discussion of his on a hadith: he said: Ṭalḥah left behind three hundred camel-loads of gold.
He narrated: سعيد بن عامر الضبعي، عن المثنى بن سعيد قال:
A man came to ʿĀʾishah bint Ṭalḥah and said: I saw Ṭalḥah in a dream, and he said:
Tell ʿĀʾishah to move me from this place, for the seeping water has harmed me.
So she rode out with her retinue, and they erected a structure over him and dug him up.
He said: Nothing of him had changed except a few hairs on one side of his beard - or he said: his head - and between the two events there were some thirty-odd years.
al-Masʿūdī related that it was his daughter ʿĀʾishah who saw the dream.
His killing was in the year 36 AH, in Jumādā al-Ākhirah.
It was also said: in Rajab; and he was aged 62, or thereabouts, and his grave is on the outskirts of Basra (2) .
Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr, Khalīfah ibn Khayyāṭ and Abū Naṣr al-Kalābādhī said: The one who killed Ṭalḥah was Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam.
Ṭalḥah had noble children, the best of them: Muḥammad al-Sajjād.
He was a young man, good, a devout worshipper (العابد), devoutly obedient to Allah.
He was born in the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and he too was killed on the Day of the Camel; ʿAlī grieved over him and said: His dutifulness to his father brought him down. ⟦1:40⟧
